Mahmud_Barzanji.title: Mahmud Barzanji
Mahmud_Barzanji.extract: Sheikh Mahmud Barzanji, also known as Mahmud Hafid Zadeh was a Kurdish leader of a series of Kurdish uprisings against the British Mandate of Iraq. He was sheikh of a Qadiriyah Sufi family of the Barzanji clan from the city of Sulaymaniyah, which is now in Kurdistan Region. He was named King of Kurd

Abdurrahman_Sharafkandi.title: Abdurrahman Sharafkandi
Abdurrahman_Sharafkandi.extract: Abdurrahman Sharafkandi, known by his pen name Hazhar, was a renowned Kurdish writer, poet, lexicographer, linguist, and translator. He was born in Mahabad, Iran.

Hemin_Mukriyani.title: Hemin Mukriyani
Hemin_Mukriyani.extract: Seyed Mohammad-Amin Shaikholislami Mukri, better known by his pen name Hemin Mukriyani or Hêmin Mukriyanî (1921–1986) was a Kurdish poet, journalist, translator, and literary critic.

Hemin.title: Hemin
Hemin.extract: Hemin is an iron-containing porphyrin with chlorine that can be formed from a heme group, such as heme B found in the hemoglobin of human blood.

Mahwi.title: Mahwi
Mahwi.extract: Mahwi (1830-1906) was one of the most prominent classical Kurdish poets and sufis from Kurdistan of Iraq. He studied in Sablakh and Sanandaj in Iranian Kurdistan. He became a judge in the court of Slemani, in today's Iraq, in 1862, which was then part of the Ottoman Empire. He travelled to Istanbul

Yashar_Kemal.title: Yaşar Kemal
Yashar_Kemal.extract: Yaşar Kemal was a leading Turkish writer of Kurdish descent, who wrote in Turkish and a human rights activist. He received 38 awards during his lifetime and had been a candidate for the Nobel Prize in Literature on the strength of his 1955 novel Memed, My Hawk.

Mehmed_Uzun.title: Mehmed Uzun
Mehmed_Uzun.extract: Mehmed Uzun was a Kurdish writer and novelist born in Siverek, Şanlıurfa Province, Turkey. Though the Kurdish language was outlawed in Turkey from 1920 to 1990, he started to write in it and achieved much toward shaping a modern Kurdish literary language and reviving the Kurdish tradition of storyte

Ahmed_Arif.title: Ahmed Arif
Ahmed_Arif.extract: Ahmed Arif was a Turkish-Kurdish poet.

Bachtyar_Ali.title: Bachtyar Ali
Bachtyar_Ali.extract: Bachtyar Ali, is a Kurdish novelist, intellectual, literary critic, essayist, and poet. Ali started out as a poet and essayist, but has established himself as an influential novelist from the mid-1990s. He has published thirteen novels, and several collections of poetry and essays.

Mehrdad_Izady.title: Mehrdad Izady
Mehrdad_Izady.extract: Michael Mehrdad R.S.C. Izady or Michael Izady, a contemporary writer on ethnic and cultural topics, particularly the Greater Middle East, and Kurds.

Refik_Saydam.title: Refik Saydam
Refik_Saydam.extract: İbrahim Refik Saydam was a Turkish physician, politician and the fourth Prime Minister of Turkey, serving from 25 January 1939 until his death on 8 July 1942.

Musa_Anter.title: Musa Anter
Musa_Anter.extract: Musa Anter, also known as "Apê Musa", was a Kurdish writer, journalist and intellectual. Anter was assassinated by Turkish JITEM in September 1992.

Mehmet_Uzun.title: Mehmet Uzun
Mehmet_Uzun.extract: Mehmet Uzun is a Turkish former freestyle wrestler. He won the silver medal in the men's freestyle 82 kg event at the 1974 World Wrestling Championships and gold medals at the 1971 Mediterranean Games and the 1975 Mediterranean Games. He also competed at the 1976 Summer Olympics, where he finished f

Hejar.title: Abdurrahman Sharafkandi
Hejar.extract: Abdurrahman Sharafkandi, known by his pen name Hazhar, was a renowned Kurdish writer, poet, lexicographer, linguist, and translator. He was born in Mahabad, Iran.

Sheikh_Said_Piran.title: Sheikh Said
Sheikh_Said_Piran.extract: Sheikh Said was a Zaza Kurd religious leader, one of the leading sheikhs of the Naqshbandi order and the head of the Sheikh Said rebellion.

Salim_(Kurdish_poet).title: Salim (poet)
Salim_(Kurdish_poet).extract: Salim is the pen name for Abdul-Rehman Begi Saheb-Qiran the nineteenth century Kurdish poet. Known by his pseudonym as Salim or Salem, he was born around 1800 in Sulaymaniyah, Kurdistan and died 1866. He is one of the most significant classical Kurdish poets who wrote in Central Kurdish. He was the

Foad_Mostafa_Soltani.title: Foad Mostafa Soltani
Foad_Mostafa_Soltani.extract: Foad Mostafa Soltani was one of the founders of the Revolutionary Organisation of the Toilers of Kurdistan, popularly known as Komala.

Ehmedê_Xasî.title: Ehmedê Xasî
Ehmedê_Xasî.extract: Ehmedê Xasî was a Kurdish literary figure and Mufti. He is best known for his work Mewlîdu'n-Nebîyyî'l-Qureyşîyyî from 1899 which is considered the first literary work in Zaza.

Abdullah_Çatlı.title: Abdullah Çatlı
Abdullah_Çatlı.extract: Abdullah Çatlı was a Turkish secret government agent, as well as a contract killer for the National Intelligence Organization (MİT). He led the Grey Wolves, the youth branch of the Nationalist Movement Party (MHP), during the 1970s. His death in the Susurluk car crash, while travelling in a car wit

Leyla_Zana.title: Leyla Zana
Leyla_Zana.extract: Leyla Zana is a Kurdish politician in Turkey. She was imprisoned for ten years for her political activism, which was deemed by the Turkish courts to be against the unity of the country. She was awarded the 1995 Sakharov Prize by the European Parliament but was unable to collect it until her release

Aziz_Mahmud_Hudayi.title: Aziz Mahmud Hudayi
Aziz_Mahmud_Hudayi.extract: Aziz Mahmud Hüdayi (1541–1628), was one of the most renowned Sufi saints of the Ottoman Empire. A mystic, poet, composer, and influential Hanafi-Maturidi scholar, he served as a spiritual advisor to several

Cemal_Nebez.title: Jamal Nebez
Cemal_Nebez.extract: Jamal Nebez was a Kurdish linguist, mathematician, politician, author, translator and writer. He studied Islamic law, philosophy, theology, physics and mathematics at the University of Baghdad in the 1950s. In 1956, he prepared a stenciled script on algebra and in 1960, succeeded in publishing the f

Ihsan_Nuri.title: Ihsan Nuri
Ihsan_Nuri.extract: Ihsan Nuri, also known as Ihsan Nuri Pasha, 1892 or 1893, Bitlis – 25 March 1976, Tehran) was a Kurdish soldier and politician, former officer of the Ottoman and Turkish Army, and one of the leaders of the Ararat rebellion as the generalissimo of the Kurdish National Forces.

Simko_Shikak.title: Simko Shikak
Simko_Shikak.extract: Ismail Agha Shikak, also known as Simko, was a Kurdish chieftain of the Shekak tribe. He was a warlord who controlled significant land and led thousands of Kurdish rebels who defeated the Qajar and Pahlavi armies on several occasions. He had also fought against the Ottomans and other foreign troops

Nizamettin_Ariç.title: Nizamettin Ariç
Nizamettin_Ariç.extract: Nizamettin Ariç is a contemporary Kurdish singer, composer and director. He was exposed to traditional Kurdish bard music or dengbêj at an early age, but until 1980 was professionally active as a singer of Turkish-language folksongs, including songs that he himself had translated from Kurdish to Tur

Şakiro.title: Şakiro
Şakiro.extract: Şakir Deniz, also known as Şakiro, was a Kurdish Dengbêj singer.

Karapetê_Xaço.title: Karapetê Xaço
Karapetê_Xaço.extract: Karapetê Xaço or Karabêtê Xaço or Gerabêtê Xaço, was an Armenian singer of traditional Kurdish Dengbêj music.

Mihemed_Şêxo.title: Mihemed Şêxo
Mihemed_Şêxo.extract: Mihemed Şêxmûs Salih better known as Mihemed Şêxo, was one of the most important Kurdish folk singers. With his sentimental, traditional and often political lyrics he created great Kurdish music like few before him. His work is still well-known and listened to today.

Yıldız_Tilbe.title: Yıldız Tilbe
Yıldız_Tilbe.extract: Yıldız Tilbe is a Turkish singer and one of the best-selling musical artists in Turkey, known especially for her eastern-infused ballads.

Aynur_Doğan.title: Aynur Doğan
Aynur_Doğan.extract: Aynur Doğan is a contemporary Kurdish singer and musician from Turkey.

Rojda.title: Rojda
Rojda.extract: Rojda is a contemporary Kurdish singer.

Diyar_Dersim.title: Diyar Dersim
Diyar_Dersim.extract: Diyar Yıldırım knows as Diyar Dersim is a Kurdish singer. During 2015 Turkey general elections, he supports HDP, pro-Kurdish party in Turkey, He sings with the party cochairman Selahattin Demirtaş as a part of campaigning the election.

Ferhat_Tunç.title: Ferhat Tunç
Ferhat_Tunç.extract: Ferhat Tunç Yoslun is a singer of Türkish descent.

Sivan.title: Sivan
Sivan.extract: Sivan is the ninth month of the civil year and the third month of the religious year on the Hebrew calendar. It is a month of 30 days. Sivan usually falls in May–June on the Gregorian calendar.

Ferzende_Beg.title: Ferzende
Ferzende_Beg.extract: Ferzende or Ferzende Beg, was a Kurdish Heseni tribesman, soldier and politician.

Selahattin_Demirtaş.title: Selahattin Demirtaş
Selahattin_Demirtaş.extract: Selahattin Demirtaş is a Kurdish politician, lawyer and author. He was the co-leader of the left-wing pro-Kurdish Peoples' Democratic Party (HDP), serving alongside Figen Yüksekdağ from 2014 to 2018. Selahattin Demirtaş announced that he left politics after the May 2023 elections.

Ahmet_Türk.title: Ahmet Türk
Ahmet_Türk.extract: Ahmet Türk is a Kurdish politician from the Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party. He has been a member of the Grand National Assembly of Turkey for several terms and was elected thrice as the Mayor of Mardin.
